_comment: Training inputs — train + val data with labels. Three layers: `items` = what the code needs (schema, survives moving machines); `candidates` = what is actually available here and how well each fits (machine-specific, re-scan after rsync); `sources` = which candidate a given run chose (snapshotted per run). Actual files stored in stages/training/data/.

candidates._comment:
Per item name, an ordered list of usable options found by /train-init. Entry: {location, path, match, notes, evidence?, host?, scanned_at?, needs?, resolve?}. location: code_default | local | s3 | server:<key> | downloadable | handoff:<handoff_id> | dataset:<id>@<snapshot> — this determines how /train-run uses it (use directly / download / run ON that machine / reference only / wait for someone else / resolve a frozen snapshot). match: ok | mismatch | absent | pending | unreachable. The code_default entry (the original author's path) must be listed even when absent — it is the reference for directory layout and the yardstick for judging the others. Search order: code-declared + local + downloadable are done by default; S3 and remote servers are slow and need credentials, so ask first.

`dataset:<id>@<snapshot>` is a CITATION, not a path, and is the option to prefer when it exists: it names a frozen membership set rather than whatever is in a directory today. Its `path` stays empty and it carries a `resolve` block {dataset, snapshot, at, layers} instead — `census.py resolve` turns that into openable paths per run, written into the RUN dir. Never store the resolved paths here: they embed one machine's root, and this config outlives that machine. The run cites `datasets/<id>@<snapshot>` in run.json -> lineage.parents, same slot as `handoffs/<id>`.

ground_truth._comment: Labels paired with each input split (train / val).

preprocessing._comment: The transform chain applied to inputs before the model sees them. CROSS-STAGE CONTRACT: normalization / input_layout / label_transform must match between training and eval/infer — a mismatch trains and infers without error and silently degrades production output. augmentation is train-only; its presence in an eval/infer stage is a bug. Every block carries `evidence` (path:line) because these values are read out of code, not declared anywhere.
